articleTitle: Impact of ChatGPT and the Capability to Critically Use Technological Creativity on English Proficiency of High School Student
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence technology, such as ChatGPT, into learning management represents a significant advancement beyond the confines of traditional education. This study aims to compare the effects of using ChatGPT on the English proficiency of high school students. The variable of interest is the capability to critically use technological creativity, which serves as a common factor in education. The research employs a causal-comparative approach with a sample group consisting of 93 high school students from the school under the supervision of Suranaree University of Technology, Thailand. The findings reveal that the capability to critically use technological creativity significantly influences students' English proficiency. Data analysis using one-way ANCOVA tests indicates that students who utilized ChatGPT for English learning demonstrated lower English proficiency compared to those who did not use ChatGPT.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Analysis Review of Serious Games Learning in Augmented Reality Education
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: As a technological innovation, augmented reality has gained significant attention within the educational sphere due to its potential to transform learning experiences. Serious games, which combine educational objectives with gaming elements, represent a promising approach to leveraging augmented reality technology for instructional purposes. However, few literature reviews have been analyzed by using bibliometric methods in the past. In this article, a bibliometric analysis of the field of serious games education within the AR domain over the past decade is conducted using Biblioshiny from RStudio, which was employed to categorize and evaluate the contributions of authors, countries, Institutions, and journals, visualize their collaboration networks, and explores the temporal evolution of research output.

articleTitle: A Drawing Accuracy Evaluation Method with Localized Normalized Cross-Correlation for Portrait Drawing Learning Assistant System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: Nowadays, portrait drawing has gained popularity from various advantages in human sentiment cultivations and digital technology progresses including a tablet or a PC. However, it is still difficult for novices to get started from scratch. Previously, we have developed the Portrait Drawing Learning Assistant System (PDLAS) to assist portrait drawing by providing auxiliary lines as a reference. They are generated by running OpenPose and OpenCV to extract facial features. However, a method of evaluating the drawing accuracy is not implemented in PDLAS. In this paper, we present a drawing accuracy evaluation method of calculating the Normalized Cross-Correlation (NCC) for each face part to quantify the similarity between a user draw and its original face image. By localizing the range for each part, the result is improved. In the evaluation section, we analyze the scores assigned to different facial features by the NCC and identify the issues revealed by the scores for each user. Furthermore, we provide suggestions for improvement based on the weaknesses found in the users. Thus, we can provide specific feedback to the users.

articleTitle: A Study of Code Typing Problems as Start-Up Programming Practices in Java Programming Learning Assistant System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: In many universities around the world, Java is popularly used for teaching basic programming to novice students. To accommodate this reality, we have developed Java Programming Learning Assistant System (JPLAS) as a self-study tool. JPLAS offers several types of exercise problems that have different learning goals and difficulty levels. However, they assume that learners are familiar with a code editor to type programming code, although they may be first-year undergraduate students and have no experience. In this paper, we present the Code Typing Problem (CTP) as a new type in JPLAS to help them practice code typing in an editor. CTP has two levels of exercises, namely, basic and advanced, to enhance its usage. The basic CTP requests to type the given code as it is in input forms. The advanced CTP gives a code with several errors of incorrect elements and requests to type the corrected code by understanding the grammar and behaviour. The error injection algorithm is presented to add errors in a code automatically. For evaluations, we generated 17 basic and 6 advanced CTP instances, and assigned them to 21 second-semester and 46 first-semester students in State Malang Polytechnic, Indonesia. Their answer results showed that most students solved all the instances correctly, which confirms the validity. However, as the number of solving students decreased in the advanced CTP, improvements will be necessary in future works.

articleTitle: Development of Programming Materials for Recurrent Education Among Working People
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: These days, there is a growing interest in re-learning among working people, and the importance of recurrent education as lifelong education is increasing. This research establishes a basis for creating an environment in which people can continue to learn even after they have entered the workforce. The purpose of this study is to propose a function to facilitate access to on-demand programming materials for recurrent education. The proposed function is a recommendation function that can recommend contents suitable for each learner. This recommendation function will be created as an extension of the on-demand environment, and learners will be able to leverage it to learn programming, improve their programming skills, and, consequently, enhance their learning efficiency. Future work includes improving the recommendation function for greater accuracy and conducting further validation to bolster reliability.

articleTitle: Game Scrum: Reinventing the Agile Methodology Through Computer Game Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: Computer games are challenging to develop because they are complex and volatile. Creating a single game requires a combination of skills. In this research, the researcher wanted to test game development using the Scrum method, a systematic work process designed to accomplish complex tasks through effective teamwork. The researcher used the game development project ‘Ya Mo City: The Legendary Adventure’ as a case study, employing the Scrum method in the game creation process. The results of the satisfaction assessment of the experimental group, consisting of 100 people, showed that the overall satisfaction of the testers with the game was at a good level, with a mean of 4.06 and a standard deviation of 0.81.

articleTitle: A Web-Based Recommender Application for Board Games Using OOP Design
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: Today, board games are widely used for educational purposes. Scope of board games used in education covers various fields such as history, strategy, economy, and military. In this paper, we present an Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) design and online implementation of a web-based recommender application for board games, employing three popular recommendation techniques. The proposed system employs item-based collaborative filtering, user-based collaborative filtering, and content-based recommendation. We design the system's architecture exploiting OOP concepts such as inheritance and polymorphism. By utilizing OOP concepts, the proposed system achieves modularity, extensibility, and maintainability, harnessing three recommendation techniques in a compact structure. To the best of our knowledge, such a modular design for the conventional recommendation techniques has not been presented previously. Additionally, we implemented a data preprocessing pipeline to ensure the system's readiness for online deployment with the board games dataset. This pipeline encompasses strategic data design, data cleaning, and transformative data handling procedures. As a result, our system handles information retrieval from a vast dataset comprising approximately 19 million ratings for over 20,000 games. By integrating three different methodologies in the system, we aim to present a variety of game recommendations for educators, but for also board game players as well.

articleTitle: OpenPose Based Poses Difficulty Assessment by 6-Keypoint Body Area for Yoga Self-Practice System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: In this study, the proposed approach involves by using a 6-point body area assessment to enhance the difficulty classification of the Yoga self-practice system and guide users through self-training during Yoga sports. This study introduces not only the calculation of the shoelace area for Yoga poses but also proposes to use the spinal skeleton as a symmetry line by dividing the body into left and right halves for assessing symmetry and regularity in the shapes, addressing the balance required for Yoga poses. This work explores how to utilize key point information from OpenPose by calculating 6-point body area and measuring the difficulty of various Yoga poses through symmetry lines. The analysis of Yoga pose difficulty is crucial for user's experiences. Finally, the parameters through the calculations of body area demonstrate the differences in shape, symmetry, and regularity in 6-point body areas. The experimental results reveal that the body-area based analysis facilitates the definition of the difficulty classification and functional enhancement for Yoga self-practice system.

articleTitle: Designing an AR-Based Guidance and Feedback System for Learning Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: Nowadays, courses rely mainly on traditional teaching materials to conduct learning activities, through which learners are guided by instructors to learn new concepts meaningfully and integrate and structure course contents efficiently. On the other hand, the localization and marked concept identification of augmented reality (AR), incorporated into study guides for learning activities and suitable teaching strategies, can also help learners grasp and follow an effective learning structure more easily. This study proposed the use of an AR-based Guidance and Feedback (ARGF) system to assist learning and, supplemented by teaching materials and health education course contents at the senior elementary level, to allow learners to interact with the materials and contents through the AR learning navigation system. The research results revealed that ARGF was effective in improving the learners' academic performance.

articleTitle: Implementation and Analysis of Multi-Objective Task Unloading Optimization Algorithm for Vehicular Edge Computing Load Balance
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: In the Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) system, the task offloading decision for delay optimization can minimize the total time consumption between end users and edge server during the offloading process. Consider the mobility of vehicular users, developing appropriate task offloading strategies poses certain challenges. Due to the characteristics of vehicle units gathering and disbanding in a short period of time in the VEC service coverage, a large number of vehicle tasks offloading causes the overload of nearest MEC servers. In this research, we implement the Multi-objective Task Unloading Optimization (MTUOA-LP) algorithm, which includes Load Prediction based on LSTM Neural Network Model using Adaptive Genetic Algorithm (LP-AGA-LS) and Multi-objective Task Unloading Optimization based on Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III to perform load balancing of VEC servers. The LP-AGA-LS establishes a load prediction algorithm of computing resources for VEC servers in order to improve the accuracy of computing resource prediction. And the LP-AGA-LS designs a task offloading strategy with the goal of time delay with VEC server load balancing to construct a multi-objective optimization model. Based on our experimental results, we can say that the MTUOA-LP algorithm can optimize task latency, achieve significant advantages in load balancing, and solve the problem of imbalanced load on MEC servers.

articleTitle: An Enhanced AES256 Key Generation Process with Keccak-F Permutation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: Amidst the escalating cybersecurity challenges of 2023, our study introduces an innovative method to strengthen AES256 encryption by integrating the Keccak-f permutation into the key generation process. Validated by NIST SP 800–22, our approach enhances AES 256's resilience against evolving threats. We developed a web application for data encryption and decryption to showcase the practical applicability and effectiveness of our method in securing digital data. In our evaluation, five battery tests prioritize detecting general randomness properties, spatial correlations, and systematic biases or patterns in the cipher bitstream of five images. The obtained results show average p-values for each test: Frequency Test (0.808516), Block Frequency (0.4973584), Serial Test (0.4083832), Runs Test (0.7673616), and Non-overlapping Template Test (0.4176802). In the context of randomness of sequences, a p-value greater than the significance level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> of 0.01 (1%) suggests that the observed sequence is consistent with randomness. Moreover, the computed average Shannon Entropy (0.921106626) implies that the bitstream is fairly unpredictable. Our results underscore promising heightened data security. The enhanced AES 256 algorithm has great potential for securing sensitive data across diverse domains like secure messaging, blockchain networks, and IoT devices. This innovation strengthens AES 256's resilience against evolving threats, promising heightened data protection and addressing critical cybersecurity challenges in the digital realm.

articleTitle: TopicShare: An AI and ChatGPT-Based Data Sharing Framework on Teaching Content in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: In higher education, information asymmetry significantly affects instructional efficacy and curriculum development. Syllabi are meant to clearly guide students and instructors, often confuse due to unclear course content. This leads to redundant material coverage and missed opportunities for new content, impacting learning and operational efficiency. Our study introduces a novel framework to improve syllabus data sharing among higher education stakeholders. By using the advanced capabilities of ChatGPT and AI, our framework named “Top-icShare” analyzes syllabi to extract essential teaching content, such as course topics, prerequisites, and textbooks. The extracted data is then presented through an intuitive data visualization interface, enhancing the comprehensibility and accessibility of syllabus content. We implemented our framework as a pilot within the Decision and System Sciences Department at a US-based university. This implementation served primarily to test the feasibility of the framework by creating a visualization platform and successfully extracting accurate information from syllabi. The pilot demonstrated that our framework significantly enhances the clarity and usability of syllabi, providing faculty with actionable insights that help refine their courses. These results affirm that our approach can help faculties share learning content, thereby promoting a more collaborative and efficient educational environment. The experiments' data visualization results can be found at: Data Visualization Page

articleTitle: Towards Precision in Educational Testing: Automated Question Creation and Difficulty Assessment in CAT-CBT
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: Recent educational advancements spotlight the integration of Item Response Theory (IRT) into computer adaptive testing (CAT) for computer-based testing (CBT). This paper demonstrates the necessity of generating diverse questions with controlled difficulty levels to avoid floor and ceiling effects, emphasizing the automation of question creation and pre-assessment of difficulties. Our study contrasts questions based on selecting fitting versus non-fitting examples, discovering that non-fitting example questions pose greater difficulty. Building on this insight, we propose a method to double the CAT item pool by automatically generating non-fitting example questions from human-crafted fitting example questions. This approach not only enriches the diversity of the item pool but also demonstrates its effectiveness in enhancing the robustness of CAT systems.

articleTitle: A New Approach for an Introduction to Computer Networking Course: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Technology and Education Technology (ITET)
abstract: The course Introduction to Computer Networks (ICN) has become one of the most vital courses in Computer Science and Software Engineering degrees and clearly is an imperative course for a degree in computer networking. However, despite its importance, the course suffers from many issues which lead to a high failure rate and low success. Even students who pass the course have problems understanding key concepts in data communication. One of the key issues is the theoretical nature of the material of the course. Many of the concepts are abstract and dry, which the students find hard to understand and boring. At the Jerusalem College of Technology (JCT), we encountered such problems with our networking course. We therefore decided to suspend the course for a year, research successful networking courses, and apply our findings to a revised networking course. One of the strategic changes that was made was to introduce more practical material into the course. Top-down approach to networking replaced a bottom-up approach, hands-on lab were added to the course, and online quizzes were included. This paper presents some of our findings and changes that were made to the networking course. The problems that were present in our original version of the ICN course are not unique to the JCT but are common to networking courses throughout higher education institutions. We therefore believe that the findings of our research can benefit other faculty who wish to improve their networking courses.
